name: Webhook Signature Verifier API
shortDescription: Deterministic HMAC webhook signature verification with presets for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, and Svix
description: Agent-native webhook signature verification computed with real cryptography (Node crypto HMAC + constant-time compare), not a language model. /verify takes a provider preset (stripe, github, shopify, slack, svix, or generic), the signing secret, the raw request body, and the signature header value, then reconstructs that provider's exact signed string, computes the digest, and compares it in constant time — returning signature_status (valid, invalid, missing_signature, missing_timestamp), the computed_signature, algorithm/encoding, and a concrete recommended_fix when it fails. The one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object (why_result_generated, key_factors, invalidators) and prioritized recommended actions. Handles Stripe's t=…,v1=… timestamped scheme, GitHub sha256= hex, Shopify base64, Slack v0:ts:body, and Svix/standard-webhooks id.ts.body base64. Secrets and payloads are never stored; results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0.

name: Webhook Reliability Scorer API
shortDescription: Deterministic webhook delivery-health score from an attempt log or aggregate stats — score, rates, latency, retry policy
description: Agent-native webhook delivery-health scoring computed in real arithmetic (not by a language model). /score accepts either a raw attempt log (each with success, status_code, latency_ms, attempt_number) or aggregate stats (total/successful/retried deliveries plus optional latency summary and failure breakdown) and returns a 0–100 delivery_score, a health_status (healthy, degraded, unhealthy, critical), success/failure/retry rates, p50/p95/max latency, a failure breakdown by category (client_error, server_error, timeout, connection_error), and a recommended retry policy tuned to the dominant failure mode. The one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object (why_result_generated, key_factors, invalidators) and prioritized recommended actions. Results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0; nothing is stored.

name: Webhook Validator API
shortDescription: Deterministic webhook config + payload best-practice checklist — HTTPS, signature, replay, idempotency, timeouts, JSON
description: Agent-native webhook best-practice validation computed by real rule-based checks (not a language model). /validate accepts any subset of webhook configuration fields — endpoint url, signature verification, timestamp/replay protection, idempotency, content-type, handler timeout, retry budget, max payload size — plus an optional sample raw body, and returns a typed checks[] (each with id, severity from critical to info, pass/fail/warn status, message, and a concrete recommendation), pass/fail/warning counts, and a 0–100 validation_score with a production-readiness verdict (production_ready, needs_attention, not_production_ready). The one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object and a prioritized, severity-ordered fix list. Results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0; nothing is stored.

name: Webhook Payload Builder API
shortDescription: Build a signed webhook envelope + ready-to-send request for Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, Svix, or generic HMAC
description: Agent-native signed-webhook envelope builder computed with real cryptography (Node crypto HMAC), not a language model. /build takes a provider preset, an event_type, the payload data, and a signing secret, then serializes a canonical {id,type,created,data} JSON body, computes the HMAC signature, and returns the provider-formatted signature header(s), the timestamp and idempotency message id used, the exact signed string, and a complete ready-to-send request spec (method, url, headers, body). Supports Stripe (t=…,v1=…), GitHub (sha256=…), Shopify (base64), Slack (v0:ts:body), Svix/standard-webhooks (id.ts.body), and generic HMAC. Ideal for integration tests, replays, fixtures, and local development. The one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object and send guidance. Results are deterministic so confidence is always 1.0; secrets are never stored.
